html:
The Western Turkic Khaganate was the western half of the empire of the Göktürks, ruling the steppes and oases of Central Asia from the Altai to the Caspian. It split from the eastern half in the late 500s. The map shows its lands, from Transoxiana to the Caspian, around 700.

Its khans drew wealth from the Silk Road towns of Sogdia and from the tribes called the Ten Arrows. Under Tong Yabghu, who ruled from about 618 to 628, it was at its height: he allied with the Byzantine emperor Heraclius against the Sasanian Empire, and in 630 he received the pilgrim Xuanzang at his court near Tokmok.

After his murder the khaganate fell into civil war. The Tang dynasty defeated its last strong khan in 657 and ruled through puppet khans. By about 700 the Türgesh tribe had taken over the Ten Arrows, and the line of the Western khans ended in the 740s. Their lands passed to the Türgesh, the Karluks and, in the south, the Arabs. See also the Türk Khaganates.
